title: Payment API returns HTTP 500
diagnostic_checks: Check application logs for the request timestamp and stack trace.
Verify that payment-service dependencies are healthy and reachable.
Review recent deployments and configuration changes.
Check whether the error affects all requests or only specific request types.
known_resolution: If logs identify a recent deployment or configuration change as the cause, follow the team's rollback or correction procedure.
If a dependency is unhealthy, escalate to the owning service team and follow its recovery procedure.
notes: Do not retry payment requests blindly; first check whether the transaction was already processed.

title: Application cannot connect to database
diagnostic_checks: Confirm the database service is running and healthy.
Check the hostname, port, and connection string in the application configuration.
Verify network access, firewall rules, and DNS resolution from the application environment.
Review database connection limits and application logs.
known_resolution: Correct invalid connection settings using the approved configuration process.
If the database is unavailable or connection limits are exhausted, escalate to the Database/Infrastructure team.
notes: Never paste credentials or connection strings containing secrets into tickets or chat.

title: Users cannot log in
diagnostic_checks: Check whether the issue affects one user or multiple users.
Review authentication service status and relevant error logs.
Confirm there is no known identity-provider outage.
Check recent authentication configuration or certificate changes.
known_resolution: For a single account, follow the approved account recovery process.
For multiple users or an identity-provider issue, escalate to the Identity/Authentication team.
notes: Never ask users to share passwords, one-time codes, or recovery tokens.

title: Application response is slow
diagnostic_checks: Record the time window, affected endpoint, and scope of the issue.
Check application latency, CPU, memory, and error-rate metrics.
Review logs for slow database queries or dependency delays.
Compare the current behavior with recent deployments and traffic changes.
known_resolution: Address the bottleneck identified by metrics or logs using the team's documented procedure.
Escalate to the owning application or infrastructure team if the bottleneck is unclear or persists.
notes: Avoid restarting services without checking impact and following the team's runbook.

title: HTTP 401 or 403 response
diagnostic_checks: Confirm whether the response is 401 (authentication) or 403 (authorization).
Check token expiry, issuer, audience, and required scopes without exposing the token.
Verify the caller's role and permissions for the requested resource.
Review recent access-policy or API-gateway configuration changes.
known_resolution: Refresh credentials through the approved authentication flow if the token has expired.
Request the minimum required permission through the approved access process if authorization is missing.
notes: Do not paste access tokens, API keys, or other secrets into the assistant.

title: File upload fails
diagnostic_checks: Check the exact error message and whether all files or only certain files fail.
Verify file size and file type against the documented limits.
Check storage-service health and available capacity.
Review application and storage logs for the failed request.
known_resolution: Use an allowed file type and remain within the documented size limit.
If storage or service errors are present, escalate to the Storage/Application team.
notes: The sample environment does not define actual upload limits; verify them in the real service documentation.
